extract:
Viagra Boys are a post-punk band from Stockholm, Sweden, formed in the mid-2010s and active ever since. They emerged from the city's interconnected indie and garage scene, where several members had played in other local groups. The band is fronted by Sebastian Murphy, an American-born singer who grew up in California and moved to Sweden, where he worked as a tattoo artist before music took over. His sardonic, slurring baritone and heavily tattooed, shirtless stage persona quickly became the group's calling card.

The band coalesced around a love of grimy, repetitive grooves. They drew on the motorik pulse of krautrock, the sneering minimalism of post-punk, and the abrasive sleaze of no wave and garage rock, while a squalling saxophone gave the music a skronky, jazz-inflected edge. Early releases established the formula. The Consistency of Energy EP (2016) and the Call of the Wild EP (2017) paired lurching bass lines and droning rhythms with Murphy's deadpan tales of dissolution and masculine absurdity.

Their breakthrough came with the debut album Street Worms (2018), released on the Stockholm label YEAR0001. The single Sports became a cult favorite thanks to its relentless list-chant delivery and absurdist video, and Just Like You reinforced their reputation for bleakly comic songwriting. A deluxe edition followed in 2019. The second album, Welfare Jazz (2021), broadened their palette, with singles such as Ain't Nice and Creatures leaning into synth-driven grooves and more danceable new wave textures. The record closed with a cover of John Prine's In Spite of Ourselves, a duet with Amy Taylor of Amyl and the Sniffers that showed a warmer, more self-deprecating side. Around the same period they released a cover of Blur's Girls & Boys and the Shrimp Sessions 2 EP.

In 2021 the band suffered the loss of guitarist Benjamin Vallé, who died that year. They pressed on with Cave World (2022), preceded by the singles Ain't No Thief and Troglodyte. The album aimed its satire at conspiracy culture, online paranoia, and regressive masculinity, framing humanity as backsliding into primitive behavior. The record kept their throbbing, saxophone-laced sound while sharpening the political bite of Murphy's lyrics. Their association with YEAR0001 also tied them to a wider wave of Swedish alternative acts gaining international attention.

Critics have consistently praised the band's ability to make music that is funny, confrontational, and physically propulsive all at once. Many have singled out Murphy's caricatured portrayals of losers, bros, and burnouts as a form of self-aware critique rather than celebration. Their chaotic, sweat-soaked live shows earned them a reputation as one of Europe's most compelling live acts and led to extensive touring and festival bookings across Europe, North America, and Australia. Within the loose online taxonomy of scrappy, hyperactive punk, they are often grouped alongside acts in the egg punk and crank wave orbit, though their sound is heavier and more groove-based than many of those peers.

Viagra Boys remain active, continuing to record and tour. They have built a durable following on the strength of their satirical worldview and their singular fusion of post-punk menace and saxophone-driven swagger. They stand as one of the most distinctive guitar bands to come out of Sweden in recent years, proof that a group rooted in a local Stockholm scene can translate wry, grimy, deeply idiosyncratic music to an international audience.
title: Viagra Boys
